references.text: God forbids Noah from eating meat with blood in it, establishing the fundamental prohibition against consuming blood that is repeated in Deuteronomy 12:23.
The law commands that the blood be poured out on the ground and covered with earth, following the same principle of pouring blood on the ground as in Deuteronomy 12:23.
A strict prohibition against eating the blood of birds or animals, with the threat of being cut off from the people.
The same command not to eat the blood but to pour it out on the ground like water, with wording almost identical to Deuteronomy 12:23.
Reiterating the prohibition against eating blood because the blood is the life, and commanding that it be poured out on the ground like water.
Saul commands the people to slaughter the animals properly and let the blood drain out, in accordance with the law against consuming blood.
The Jerusalem council requires Gentile Christians to abstain from blood, showing that the prohibition against eating blood remained important in the early church.
The apostolic decree reiterates the prohibition against eating blood as one of the necessary rules for Gentile Christians.
